properties.name: Austro-Hungarian Military Cemetery Loče
properties.desc:
[[[https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Avstro-ogrsko_voja%C5%A1ko_pokopali%C5%A1%C4%8De%2C_Lo%C4%8De_6.jpg/512px-Avstro-ogrsko_voja%C5%A1ko_pokopali%C5%A1%C4%8De%2C_Lo%C4%8De_6.jpg?20241020122558]]}

In 1916, a military cemetery was arranged at Loče near Tolmin for the Austro-Hungarian soldiers who had fallen in the battles fought in the area between Mt. Vodel and Mt. Krn. Among them were also Italian and German soldiers, but were transferred by the Italians, or the Germans respectively, in the years 1938–39. Concreate headstones are symbolically placed across the cemetery and do not mark the actual graves. Only special stone headstones mark the actual graves. In the centre of the cemetery stands a monument in the form of a pyramid. It is dedicated to the fallen soldiers of the 30th Infantry Regiment of the Imperial-and-Royal Army (KuK IR n. 30). More than 3,000 fallen soldiers rest in this cemetery.

properties.name: Austro-Hungarian Military Cemetery Log pod Mangartom
Austro-Hungarian Military Cemetery Modrejce
properties.desc: Buried in the cemetery are about 1600 soldiers of the onetime Austro-Hungarian Army who were killed at the Tolmin bridgehead or on the nearby battlefields. In the centre of the cemetery stands a monument with inscription tablets. The uniform headstones do not mark the actual graves.  The inscription on the pediment of the entrance gate reads: “Ruhestätte der Helden von St. Luzia” – The Place of Rest for the Heroes of Sveta Lucija (now: Most na Soči).

properties.name: Charnel House/Ossuary
properties.desc: In the years 1936–1938 the German state built a charnel house on the location of the former military cemetery with 931 graves. The building received mortal remains of about 1,000 German soldiers who were killed on the battlefields along the Soča in the Twelfth Isonzo Battle. The building materials for the construction of this significant cultural-historical and architectural monument were transported from South Tyrol. The work was done by a German building company from Munich. The charnel house is enclosed with a stone wall and is accessible through an iron gate, made of Austrian and Italian barrels. It is constructed of stone blocks, has a steep pent roof, and a porch from which the entrance leads into the central part of the monument, the chapel. The interior of the chapel is divided with a wrought-iron latticework into two compartments. In the first one, the names of the fallen soldiers are inscribed on oak slabs, and in the other, in a gilded mosaic. In the centre of the room, there is a tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Below this room there is a tomb with the relics of the fallen. The German Charnel House is the only location in the area of the Isonzo Front where a larger number of German soldiers are buried.

properties.name: Church of the Holy Spirit in Javorca, 571 m
properties.desc:
[[https://live.staticflickr.com/65535/49013887186_9b6f9ae8f1_b.jpg|{{https://live.staticflickr.com/65535/49013887186_9b6f9ae8f1_b.jpg}}]]

The memorial church of Holy Spirit on Javorca is one of the most beautiful memorials of the World War I in Slovenia. It was erected in 1916, the specialty inside are wooden wall plates in which more than 2500 names of fallen soldiers are burnt. At the entrance, there's the inscription 'Ultra cineres hostium ira non superest' (Hate should not reach beyond the ashes of the dead).

properties.name: Farmhouse Kranjc (Turistična kmetija Kranjc)
properties.desc:
Farmhouse Kranjc (Turistična kmetija Kranjc) is located in a quiet mountain village of Koseč. The pristine nature of the area enables its visitors a well spent free time. The farm offers different size rooms:

3 double bedrooms,

3 triple bedrooms,

2 apartments for four people,

2 glamping houses for two.

 

The farm offers homemade meals (half board) and wellness among other things.

properties.name: Fort Kluže
properties.desc:
Het fort Kluže is een fort nabij Bovec in de regio Primorska in het noordwesten van Slovenië.

Het werd in 1472 als vesting tussen Bovec bij de weg naar Cave del Predil en Karinthië gebouwd. Waarschijnlijk diende het aanvankelijk als verdediging van Friuli tegen de Turken. In de loop van de 16e eeuw kwam Bovec onder Oostenrijks gezag als resultaat van de oorlogen tussen Venetië en de Habsburgers. Het werd een autonoom graafschap, maar bewaarde voorlopig de kerkelijke afhankelijkheid van Ciudad en Aquilea. Aan het eind van de 18e eeuw was het gehele bestuur Oostenrijks, en dat zou zo blijven tot 1918. In 1796-1797 trok Napoleons leger door het dal; er werd rond het fort gevochten.

In 1903 werd een deel van Bovec door brand verwoest. Dat wat nog overeind stond, werd in de Eerste Wereldoorlog kapotgeschoten, toen de Italiaans-Oostenrijkse frontlijn (Isonzofront) dwars door het dal van noord naar zuid sneed.

properties.desc: Heavy gun cavern from the WW1.

properties.name: Italian Chapel
properties.desc: The chapel in Gabrje was built in 1920 on the former Italian military cemetery by the 4th Regiment of the alpini, who were part of Italian mountain troops. Buried in the cemetery were the Italian soldiers who were killed between May 1915 and March 1916 in the battles on Mts. Mrzli vrh and Vodel. Between the two World Wars their mortal remains were transferred to the charnel house at Oslavia/Oslavje north of Gorizia/Gorica.

properties.name: Italian Chapel
properties.desc: At the edge of the field in the west part of the village Ladra stands an Italian military chapel, designed by the architect Giovanni Michelucci. It was consecrated on 30 May 1917 and served outdoor religious ceremonies. The chapel is made of worked stone. The south and the north walls have Gothic-styled windows. Attached to the southeast corner is a pulpit.

properties.name: Italian Chapel on Mt. Planica
properties.desc: Among the many surviving buildings that were built during the Isonzo Front (1915–1917) there are also sacred buildings. One of them is the Italian military Chapel of Mary, Consoler of the Afflicted or Our Lady of Consolation, also known today as the Chapel Bes. The platform on which it was built was situated at the upper edge of a larger military camp located on the saddle between Mts. Planica and Pleče.

properties.name: Kal-Čelo fort, 660 m
properties.desc:
[[https://sp-images.summitpost.org/729236.jpg?auto=format&fit=max&h=1000&ixlib=php-2.1.1&q=35&s=3000710258c8734e595e9a1389970801|{{https://sp-images.summitpost.org/729236.jpg?auto=format&fit=max&h=1000&ixlib=php-2.1.1&q=35&s=3000710258c8734e595e9a1389970801}}]]

Ruins of an important fort from the WW1. It was built in 1915 by Austro-hungarian army and was used mainly as heavy guns post. On that place an open air museum is arranged and a tourist path named Walks of Peace goes nearby.

properties.name: Kolovrat Museum of the First World War
properties.desc: The circular path through the outdoor museum Kolovrat runs past command- and observation posts, machine gun and gun positions, caves and networks of trenches and connection galleries at several levels. A visit to these positions is of special interest thanks to various details, such as, for example, spiral stairs in one of the caves, and also due to partly original materials which were used in the wartime. From the top of the Kolovrat ridge a splendid view opens over the onetime Isonzo Front battlefield, reaching from Mt. Kanin and the Krn range to Mt. Sveta Gora, and all to the Trieste Gulf.

properties.name: Monument to Riccardo Giusto
properties.desc: Under the Kolovrat ridge and near Solarie/Solarje Pass stands a monument to the Alpine soldier Riccardo Giusto, allegedly the first Italian casualty of the Isonzo Front. The monument of a flying eagle was donated by the National Alpine Corps Association (Sezione ANA) of Cividale del Friuli.

properties.name: Mt. Kozlov rob
properties.desc: The elevation Kozlov rob, which rises above Tolmin, has always been a dominant element in the Tolmin cultural landscape. Though it is beter known for its former 12th century castle, Kozlov rob played an important role at the time of the Isonzo Front too. It was a fortified observation post of the Austro-Hungarian Army, from where they shelled the Italian positions on the Tolmin bridgehead. It is possible now to ascend Kozlov rob along the history-and-nature educational trail.

properties.name: Outdoor Museum Mengore
properties.desc: A circular path through the outdoor museum Mengore runs past well-preserved and partly cleaned and restored remains of the first Austro-Hungarian line of defence. It runs past trenches, caves, memorial tablets, remains of cabins’ stone walls, a water reservoir and the monument of the onetime Austro-Hungarian military cemetery. On the top of Mengore hill, from where a splendid view of the Soča valley opens, stands a church, dedicated to the Virgin Mary, which was practically levelled during the fights along the Soča (Isonzo).

properties.name: Outdoor Museum Mrzli vrh
properties.desc:
It is possible to reach the Outdoor Museum Mrzli vrh from several directions. The easiest access runs from the village of Krn. The path gradually ascends to the mountain pasture Pretovč (1.5 hrs walk). At Pretovč, the circular path through the outdoor museum begins.
Access is also possible from the village of Zatolmin or from the direction of Polog (Javorca).

properties.name: Štoln
properties.desc:
The name of Štoln derives from the German word “der Stollen”, which means a shaft or a tunnel. It was constructed  between 1899 and 1905 in order to drain water from the lead and zinc mine at Cave del Predil/Rabelj/Raibl.

Tijdens de Eerste Wereldoorlog liep er een smalspoor elektrische spoorlijn door de tunnel, die diende voor het vervoer van vracht en mensen naar het Isonzo-front . Naar schatting werden er tijdens de Eerste Wereldoorlog bijna een half miljoen mensen en 240.000 ton voedsel, wapens en andere goederen door Štolen vervoerd [ 2 ] . De tunnel werd ook gebruikt voor het vervoer van Sloveense mijnwerkers naar de Rabelj-mijn tot ongeveer 1974 [ 3 ] , totdat er busvervoer via de Predel- pas werd geïntroduceerd . De tunnel fungeerde tevens als grenspost tussen het voormalige Joegoslavië en Italië .
